tier_reason: The project's own divan benchmarks (benchmarks/benches/lookup.rs and benchmarks/benches/generate.rs, against phf 0.11.2) are public, and benchmarks/Cargo.toml sets the bench profile to opt-level=3 with lto=true. No rustc version, CPU model or OS is stated, results exist only as PNG charts, and no independent or peer-reviewed comparison was found, so the tier is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: quickphf/README.md: "About twice as fast as phf at lookup, and more than 10 times faster at construction"; "quickphf is about twice as fast as phf at lookup, with RawPhfMap being faster than PhfMap, especially for larger hash maps." quickphf_codegen/README.md: "about 10 times faster than with phf. It can generate a 1,000,000 entry map in about 300 ms." Approximate values read from the lookup.png and generate.png charts (derived from page data): lookup at 1M keys is phf::Map ~153 ns vs PhfMap ~86 ns (~1.8x) vs RawPhfMap ~32 ns (~4.8x); at <=1k keys it is ~23 vs ~11 vs ~10 ns (~2.1x for PhfMap). Construction at 1M keys is phf ~6.2 s vs quickphf ~0.26 s (~24x), and at 500k keys ~1.9 s vs ~0.13 s (~15x). The construction ratio grows with key count.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc version not stated; benchmarks/Cargo.toml [profile.bench] opt-level = 3, lto = true; divan 0.1 harness
corrections.workload: Static compile-time maps built with the PTHash perfect-hash algorithm. benchmarks/build.rs generates u64->u64 maps (quickphf PhfMap and RawPhfMap, and phf::Map via phf_codegen) from seeded random u64 keys at 11 sizes from 5 to 1,000,000. lookup.rs (divan) times batches of 1000 random existing-key get() calls on each map. generate.rs times perfect-hash construction only (quickphf_codegen::phf::generate_phf vs phf_generator::generate_hash) at the same sizes.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark harness is public (benchmarks/benches/lookup.rs and generate.rs, divan, bench profile opt-level=3 with LTO). The CPU model, OS and rustc version are not stated, and results appear only as PNG charts with no text or CSV. Both charts date from the initial commit (e8d22e2, 2023-10-16). The current lookup.rs was changed by PR #1 (096658a, 2023-11-16) and is missing semicolons after `let mut rng = fastrand::Rng::with_seed(SEED)`, so it does not compile unmodified. CI does not catch this because benchmarks/ is excluded from the workspace. The lookup chart is labelled in ns, but each divan iteration runs 1000 lookups, so the per-lookup normalization is undocumented. The construction benchmark measures only the build-time PHF parameter search, not runtime cost. Only random u64 keys are benchmarked, with no string keys. The baseline is the phf crate (the Rust analogue of gperf-style static tables), not std::collections::HashMap.
